title: One derived grammar production
description: A single unit of derivation work. Derived in isolation from ONLY its own inputs, so the result does not depend on what was derived before it. That is what makes an AI-assisted derivation reproducible across sessions and across OMG releases. Validated on every gate by .claude/scripts/validate_state.py.

status.description: pending: planned, not derived. derived: rule written, not yet checked. verified: passes all acceptance criteria. conflict: sources disagree and adjudication is unresolved. retired: removed upstream, kept for history.

fingerprint.description: Hashes of EXACTLY the inputs that produced this rule. On a new OMG release, comparing these tells you which units carry forward untouched and which must be re-derived. This is the mechanism that makes release N+1 cheap.

inputs.description: What was in context when this unit was derived. Nothing else may be. The clause TEXT is deliberately absent — it is joined at read time from the local export, so no OMG prose enters this repository. See check_derivation_text.py.

rule.description: The derived rule, as an AST. A JSON AST rather than EBNF text so the validation oracle consumes it directly with no meta-parser. Human-readable EBNF is rendered from this, never stored alongside it.

decision.description: WHY THE RULE READS AS IT DOES, in prose, written by whoever derived it. Deliberately not an enum. A unit records the reasoning behind one production — that a clause and the Xtext agree, that an Xtext inlining was declined, that an apparent disagreement is redundant rather than contradictory. Which SOURCE won when two genuinely conflict is a different question with a different home: it is `decision` in deviations.schema.json, as one of follow_spec / follow_corpus / follow_xtext / defer, reached through the grammar-adjudicator and recorded per deviation. Keeping the two apart is why this one is free text.

evidence.description: At least one, and each must resolve: a clause that really states this production, a corpus file that really contains an instance. Evidence that merely exists is not evidence.

kind.description: clause: a specification clause citation. corpus: a file under vendor/corpus that contains an instance. xtext: a pinned pilot grammar rule, a second opinion and never on its own sufficient. deviation: an entry in deviations.json. omg_issue: a filed OMG issue — check_citations.py cannot resolve issue IDs, so verify it by fetching the page before citing it. file_id: an OMG File ID.

notes.description: Author prose only. Machine diagnostics belong in `diagnostics`, which is a separate field precisely so that a failing check can never edit what a human wrote.

left_recursion_intended.description: Set true to accept a directly left-recursive rule. Earley tolerates left recursion; a hand-written recursive-descent parser does not, so the acceptance check fails until someone states here that the recursion is deliberate. An explicit flag rather than a phrase in `notes`, because a check that sniffs prose can be satisfied by its own failure message.

acceptance.description: Deterministic checks. Written by .claude/scripts/grammar_check_unit.py, never by hand.

diagnostics.description: Why the failing acceptance checks failed. Written by grammar_check_unit.py, never by hand, replaced in full on every run and removed once the unit passes. Never merged into `notes`.

k.description: seq: ordered concatenation. alt: alternatives. opt: zero or one. star: zero or more. plus: one or more. ref: another production, which must have its own unit. kw: a literal keyword or operator, which MUST appear in keywords.json. tok: a named terminal class such as NAME or STRING_VALUE, which is lexical and has no unit.
